fact: Deputy Minister Thomas Momo Parker says Liberia is moving to EMIS 2.0 and is committed to establishing a digitized EMIS under a costed three-year EMIS Action Plan with a USD 4.5 million budget, 60% government funded.

The AU-IPED peer review report says the Ministry of Education has initiated reforms to digitise its EMIS, moving from paper-based EMIS 1.0 to a digitised, integrated EMIS 2.0, with a three-year USD 4.5 million plan proposed.
The report says the last national school census was conducted in 2022 at a cost of USD 1 million, funded by partners, with no new data collected since.
The AU-IPED record page says the review highlighted Liberia's transition from paper-based EMIS 1.0 to a digitised, integrated EMIS 2.0, with a proposed three-year USD 4.5 million action plan.

The Liberian Observer reports the Ministry of Education is seeking a real-time education data system with a central dashboard and a digitised EMIS, after a 28-29 September 2026 consultation to draft an EMIS Policy backed by a three-year EMIS Action Plan.
The Ministry said regular Annual School Census collection has resumed following interruptions after 2021, alongside the Statutory School Record System at school level.

The African Union Commission says Liberia's Ministry of Education concluded a week-long peer review and policy dialogue (1-5 September 2025) producing a costed three-year action plan to modernise its EMIS, and has initiated a GPE funding proposal for ICT upgrades.
